scenario.fault_family: access port in wrong VLAN (misdirected prompt)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8044: PC5 in Campus 1 lost its default gateway (172.16.10.254) while
PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same access switch are fine. PC5 still has link. The team
thinks switch4 -- the upstream switch that trunks Campus 1 VLANs toward mswitch0
-- must be dropping PC5's VLAN on its trunk. Please confirm the switch4 trunk
fault and identify which VLAN it is dropping.

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-switch1-pc5-wrong-vlan: switch1's eth2 (the
access port for PC5) was moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1, the unused default
VLAN. PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10 semantics, but switch1 now
bridges them into VLAN 1 -- an L2 broadcast domain with no router attached -- so
ARP for the gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (PC6/PC7/PC8) are
unaffected.

The TWIST: the ticket blames switch4's trunk. switch4 is HEALTHY -- its trunk is
carrying VLAN 10 normally, which is exactly why PC6/PC7/PC8 (also in VLAN 10, on
the same path through switch4) still reach 172.16.10.254. If switch4 were dropping
VLAN 10, ALL of those PCs would fail, not just PC5. The single-host blast radius
is the decisive tell: a trunk dropping a VLAN is a shared failure; only a
per-port (access-port) change can break exactly one host while its VLAN peers stay
up.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = switch1 (eth2 VLAN
membership). The agent must localise from evidence -- only PC5 affected, its access
port is in the wrong VLAN on switch1 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on
switch4's trunk. An agent that "confirms the switch4 trunk fault" has followed the
accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on
switch1.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scoring_axes: must-identify-access-port-wrong-vlan: PC5's access port (eth2) is in the wrong VLAN (VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10) on switch1

bonus-clears-switch4-trunk: exonerates switch4 by any valid evidence -- e.g. explicitly clearing its trunk, or demonstrating the fault is local to switch1/PC5 while other VLAN-10 hosts (PC6/PC7/PC8) work through the same trunk

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The VLAN bridge assignment on switch1's access port eth2 (the port serving pc5) is wrong. The port is a member of `br_vlan1` (the native untagged VLAN1 bridge) instead of `br_vlan10` (the VLAN10 bridge used by pc6/pc7/pc8 and the upstream gateway).

**Mechanism:** pc5's traffic egresses switch1 as untagged frames and arrives at mswitch0's physical eth2, which is a member of `br0` (the management bridge at 10.2.2.2/24), not of the VLAN10 logical interface (`vlan10`, IP 172.16.10.254). mswitch0 proxy-ARPs for 172.16.10.254 using its eth2 MAC (`4e:2e:46:3e:82:db`), so pc5 builds an ARP cache entry. However, when mswitch0 tries to reply to pc5 at 172.16.10.5, it routes out through its `vlan10` SVI with VLAN10-tagged frames, which switch1 delivers to `br_vlan10`. Since pc5 is not a member of `br_vlan10`, it never receives mswitch0's ARP requests or ICMP replies — all traffic is silently dropped. pc6, pc7, and pc8 (switch1.eth3/4/5 → `br_vlan10`) communicate directly with the VLAN10 SVI and are unaffected.

**Localization:** switch1.eth2 — the access port connected to pc5 — is assigned to `br_vlan1` instead of `br_vlan10`. The startup script declares the correct intent (`ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10`) but the live kernel state has eth2 enslaved to `br_vlan1`.

**Root cause:** switch1's access port eth2 (pc5's port) was moved to the wrong bridge domain (`br_vlan1` instead of `br_vlan10`) after startup, placing pc5 outside VLAN10 and isolating it from its gateway and all inter-VLAN destinations.

**Fix:** On switch1, run `ip link set eth2 nomaster && ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` to reassign pc5's access port to the correct VLAN10 bridge. pc5 should then ARP for 172.16.10.254, receive the correct MAC `00:01:97:e4:04:01` from mswitch0's vlan10 SVI, and restore full connectivity.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to switch1.eth2 and notes PC6/PC7/PC8 on VLAN10 remain functional (via the same trunk), thereby exonerating switch4.
The proposed fix explicitly reassigns eth2 to br_vlan10 (including a nomaster step to detach first), which achieves the expected remediation.

The agent's logs contain the necessary observations (pc5 ping failures, differing ARP entries, switch1 live bridge membership showing eth2 in br_vlan1, and mswitch0/br MACs) and the writeup's conclusions follow logically from those observations; a minor leap is asserting 'proxy-ARP' behavior but it doesn't weaken the localization. Overall the investigation justifies the diagnosis and fix.
